sections.html:
Three paths lead out of a Wichita Falls house: a broker listing, a private sale, or a cash purchase. Condition and schedule do most of the deciding. Hail or wind damage, a tired roof or long-delayed upkeep favor cash, and a house in good shape may earn more on the open market.

Wichita Falls is the Wichita County seat, on the Wichita River in North Texas near the Oklahoma line. Buyers come from across the county and from the Sheppard Air Force Base community. Much of the housing was built between the 1920s and the 1950s. Older wiring, plumbing and foundations are common, and buyers subtract those repairs from what they offer.

  • Start with the deed, any liens and your mortgage payoff.
  • Gather permit records for the roof, additions and similar work.
  • Set a listing timeline beside a cash closing date and compare.
  • Have the title company run a search for recorded liens.

The April 10, 1979 tornado cut through the southern part of Wichita Falls, destroyed twenty percent of the dwellings in town and injured more than 3,200 people. Most of the damage was repaired within three years. The city still takes roofing and other major work seriously.

Any roof replacement, and any roof repair larger than 500 square feet, calls for a city permit. The contractor is the one who must obtain it, and before the first shingle comes off. Bonding is also required of contractors who work in town.

Keep the permit on file when you sell. Buyers down the road may hesitate over major improvements, a new roof for example, that went in without approval, and missing permits can complicate an insurance claim. If your roof was replaced after a hail storm, have the permit number and the roofer's invoice ready to hand over.

Building Inspections, at 1300 Seventh Street, issues permits and does the inspections. Forms, checklists and the fee ordinance are on the city's site. Phone 940-761-7459 to reach the office.

The city gives four reasons to use a bonded contractor and pull a permit: code compliance, safety inspections, insurance coverage and the bond itself. An owner whose roof went on without a permit may find that insurance will not cover damage tied to that work. A closed permit in your paperwork answers that worry before the buyer raises it.

Check any additions, a pool or a roof replacement from your years of ownership against permit records. When a permit was left open, ask Building Inspections how to resolve it before you list. For utility questions about a specific address, the city's utility office can answer.

Eight taxing jurisdictions in the county rely on the Wichita County Tax Office to assess and collect, and the office distributes almost $120 million a year to them. Online payment, penalty and interest details, a tax estimator and a list of the units it serves are on the office website.

Texas property tax calendar for a Wichita Falls owner
DateWhat happens
January 1Appraised value is fixed and that year's tax lien takes hold
April 30Deadline for most exemption filings
May 15Final day to protest most appraisals
October 1Tax bills go in the mail
January 31Pay by this date to avoid penalty

Penalty and interest start February 1. At closing, the title company normally divides that year's tax between you and the buyer.

Homestead relief on the school tax is $140,000, plus $60,000 more for owners over 65 or disabled. It belongs to the person who qualifies and stops when you sell. A disabled veteran may qualify for larger amounts as the disability rating rises.

The Wichita County Clerk records deeds for property inside the city. Each deed must be signed and acknowledged. The first page costs $5.00 to record and each added page $4.00.

Lenders who foreclose hold the auction on a first Tuesday, after the notice has been posted and filed for three weeks. If your sale closes before that Tuesday, the lender is repaid from the proceeds and the foreclosure can stop.

sections.h2: Selling with unpermitted work or taxes owed
sections.html:
Unpermitted work does not make a sale impossible, but it changes the conversation. A cash investor will typically buy the house as it stands and lower the price to match. A buyer with a mortgage may hear questions from the lender or an inspector.

Back taxes are paid from your proceeds when the sale closes. Phone the county tax office for today's balance, then let the title company check it against its own search. The clerk's office can supply a copy of any recorded lien, so you know what has to be cleared.

Before you speak with any buyer, run through this list:

  1. Pull the recorded deed and check each owner name.
  2. Ask your lender for a payoff statement.
  3. Find permit numbers for the roof and any additions.
  4. Ask the tax office what is owed on the account.
  5. Decide how soon you must close, then judge offers by that date.

A cash sale skips the buyer's loan approval and appraisal, so the closing date depends mostly on title work. That can mean weeks rather than months.

sections.h2: Visiting the offices and closing the sale
sections.html:
Two visits cover most of what a seller needs. At Building Inspections you can learn whether permits on your property were closed out. At the tax office you can get the balance due, see whether an exemption is on the account and hear how penalty and interest work on a late bill.

Take a photo ID, a copy of your deed, and the property address or account number. Selling on behalf of a relative or an estate? Add the recorded paperwork that shows you may sign. Also write down your questions, since staff can only answer what they are asked.

On closing day, the title company collects signatures, pays off the mortgage and any unpaid tax from the proceeds, and files the new deed with the county clerk. You hand over keys once funds are released. Ask for a final settlement statement a day ahead so you can read every line before you sign.

Ask each buyer how they plan to pay, who covers closing costs and how long they need to close. Two offers with the same headline price can leave you with very different amounts once repairs, fees and waiting time are counted.

If the house is vacant, remember that insurance and utilities are still yours until the sale is done. A shorter timeline means fewer months of carrying those costs, which is one reason sellers with storm-damaged or empty houses lean toward cash.

faqs.q: Is a permit required for a roof replacement in Wichita Falls?
faqs.a: Yes, for a replacement or any repair over 500 square feet. The contractor must pull the permit before work begins and must be bonded. Call Building Inspections if you are unsure.

faqs.q: Who collects property taxes in Wichita County?
faqs.a: The Wichita County Tax Office collects for eight taxing jurisdictions in the county. Its website has pages on penalties and interest, online payment and a tax estimator.

faqs.q: Does the 1979 tornado still matter to Wichita Falls home sellers?
faqs.a: Mostly as building history. The tornado destroyed twenty percent of the city's dwellings, and the city now stresses permits on roofing and other major work. Keep permit records for any repairs.

faqs.q: What is the property tax deadline in Wichita County?
faqs.a: Taxes are due on or before January 31. Penalty and interest start February 1, and the lien for each year attaches on January 1.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Wichita Falls house with unpermitted work?
faqs.a: Yes, but a buyer or lender may ask about it. Missing permits can make future buyers cautious. Ask Building Inspections how to close an old permit before you list.
